result.reason: I found no product, free state tool or rule that kills this. Hebrew and English searches turned up no gemach-specific management or reporting software, only generic loan systems such as CAV Systems and Nortridge, and the CrediGestor extension. The Authority's online system only accepts and validates files in a fixed template; it does not prepare the data. Two things push the score down. The market is very small: about 170 licence applications are pending and only about 20 are near-ready (ice.co.il). Deadlines are also slow: the AML circular takes full effect 1.5 years after final publication, and licensees get 2 years after licensing (Calcalist). On top of that, donation-funded bodies have limited willingness to pay, and charedi accountants or Nedarim Plus could act as competitors or channels. I didn't check either of them.

result.competitor: I found no Israeli software that produces or files the Registrar's verbal or financial report. Hebrew searches returned only Green Invoice explainers, ICPAS (Israeli accountants' institute) circulars and foreign Capterra lists. Filing goes through the Registrar's free online form, and the audited financial statements are prepared by CPAs and bookkeepers. In practice that is the existing service, and software cannot replace the CPA audit. I did not search for specific vendor names such as Hashavshevet or Rivhit add-ons, so a local accounting add-on may exist that I missed.
result.duty: The duty is real and recurs every year. Under the Associations Law and the Associations (Forms) Regulations, each association files a financial report, a verbal (narrative) report and supporting documents through the Registrar's online form. The deadline is 30 June of the year after the report year. Section 38 requires two board members to sign the reports. The proper-management certificate depends on full filing and payment of the annual fee. Without it the association cannot get state support or offer donors the s.46 tax credit. The Registrar does enforce this: in January 2025 it revoked the certificate of about 200 associations and public-benefit companies (חל"צ) for failing to file (Maariv). A Bhol article dated 23 July 2026 says the Registrar changed how the certificate is granted after public comment. I could not open it (403), so the changes are unverified. I found no specific fine amount.
result.market: About 37,000 registered associations (Atlas estimate for 2022), or 39,327 per an undated Ministry of Justice figure cited by Calcalist. About 10,000 are very active. GuideStar's 2018 yearbook counted 15,847 associations and 622 public-benefit companies that filed reports. Most are small and volunteer-run.
result.reason: The duty is real, annual, enforced, and blocks grants and the s.46 donor tax credit, so the pain is genuine. But the hard part, audited financial statements, legally needs a CPA, and the filing channel is a free state online form. The software could only help with the verbal report, the document checklist and deadline tracking, while the CPA who already serves the association owns the relationship. Small volunteer associations have little money and are hard to reach. Searches found no direct Israeli competitor, but the work is already bundled into accountants' fees. The 2026 changes to the certificate process are unverified. If they add new documentation, the opening could get somewhat bigger.

coverage.category: Business-licensing regime specifics: Kashrut (rabbinate) certificates for restaurants, caterers and food shops, plus the Tourism Ministry's licensing of tour guides, travel agents and tour operators
coverage.found: Kashrut: the Kashrut Fraud Prevention Law gives the Chief Rabbinate council, delegated to local rabbinates, sole power to certify. Applications go to the local rabbinate with Health Ministry approvals and a fee. The 2021 reform (private kashrut corporations) was repealed by the Knesset (final vote 46-41, per Maariv/Srugim reports; date unconfirmed), so no new regime-change deadline exists. The local renewal procedure was not found. Tour guides: renewal is online on gov.il, with one training day per year and a fee every two years (2025-26 payment opened 15 Dec 2024). An older article says two training sessions every two years, which conflicts; the gov.il page governs. Travel agents and inbound operators: no current licence-renewal or guarantee rules found (only State Comptroller reports from 2004-07). gov.il tour-guide page blocked (403) on fetch.

coverage.category: Alcohol, tobacco and fuel excise: small retailers and importers (Law for Licensing Sale of Intoxicating Liquor, wholesale and import licences; 2025-26 sugar/beverage and e-cigarette tax changes)
coverage.found: Alcohol: found only the Tax Authority renewal for registered ethyl-alcohol (כוהל) dealers (Purchase Tax form 50, free, file 2 months before expiry, accountant certificate on books and stock ledger). That is industrial alcohol, a tiny group. No 2025 reform of beverage-sale licensing found (older relaxations: police approval dropped for restaurants/pubs). Tobacco/vape: new purchase-tax order on e-liquid and disposables (270% of wholesale price plus 8.16 NIS/ml, floor 15.64 NIS/ml, replaces the Nov 2021 order). A stock tax of 0.84 NIS/ml on wholesaler inventory was approved in committee earlier (date unverified). A mid-2026 proposal would tax vaping devices and lower the e-liquid tax. A July 2026 Globes report says the Tax Authority collects almost nothing. Package warnings are mandatory from 2 Aug 2026. Chapter 12 of the 2026 Arrangements Law is titled 'Supervision of Smoking Products for Tax Purposes' (WTO notice, Jan 2026), but I could not read its text and could not tell whether it licenses retailers. Knesset PDF redirected (maintenance page); hon.co.il article gave no duty details.

coverage.category: Pesticide and fertiliser dealers, plant-protection permits and farm inputs (Plant Protection Law, the Ministry of Agriculture's Plant Protection and Inspection Services (שה"ה), the Israeli Standards Institution)
coverage.found: No Israeli source found for a mandatory digital pesticide-use logbook or a 'farmer to exporter' reform; the two first-search queries returned US/foreign results. Old rules found: applicator licence, buyer purchase permit, sale licence, ledger retention. The 2014 Environmental Health report notes a draft applicator-licensing bill (outcome unknown), and Adam Teva v'Din criticised the 2018 draft rules. Export residue/GlobalG.A.P-style duties come from buyers, not a confirmed state register. The C13 e-phyto and packing-house item stays unverified: no search reached it.

coverage.category: Employers' mandatory duties to workers (pension fund, severance, work-safety and the foreign-worker sector) for very small employers: the Pension Extension Order, the Minimum Wage law (April 2026 update), and the Hours of Work and Rest Law
coverage.found: Online reporting of pension and fund deposits to the managing company is mandatory by employer size. Employers with 3-9 employees: from 19 Feb 2023. Employers with fewer than 3: from 1 Feb 2025. Enforcement grace for 9 or fewer ended 1 June 2024. A narrow exemption exists for up to 5 employees with standing orders and unchanged amounts. The Capital Market Authority can fine. The duty is real but sits with payroll software, the employers interface and bureaus. No 2025-27 wage-slip or minimum-wage detail found. The kolzchut page was blocked (403), so the details come from search snippets.

coverage.category: Vehicle-related small-operator regimes: driving-school and driving-test centres, tow-truck, truck-fleet and motor-testing stations (מכונים לבדיקת רכב), and the new Ministry of Transport rules on e-bikes and scooters sellers
coverage.found: Carrier licence: apply or renew with the Transport Supervisor via gov.il; renewal opens about 1.5 months before expiry. Operators with up to 5 vehicles need a carrier-training course; 6 or more need a certified professional manager. Business licence is needed for some haulage types. Digital tachograph: July 2026 reports say regulations are advancing for new heavy trucks and buses, with the final text unverified. E-bikes and scooters: owners must register and display a plate (fine 100 NIS from 1 Sep 2024, 500 from 1 Sep 2025, 750 from 1 Sep 2026). Importers need Transport Ministry commercial import approval and a SII mark under standard SI 15194; SII's special conditions for manufacturers are dated 29 Jul 2025. In July 2026 customs arrested an importer of more than 1,000 non-compliant e-bikes. I found no duty on shops to register vehicles before sale. gov.il carrier page blocked (403). Driving schools, tow operators and test centres not searched.

coverage.category: Environmental and municipal duties for small operators: municipal business tax (ארנונה) and the Packaging Law deposit regime, waste-collection fees, and the clean-air rules for gas-engine and boiler emissions
coverage.found: Clean Air Law 2008: emission permits are required for listed sources. Smaller sources are regulated through business-licence conditions. A 2023 report mentions a plan to merge four permits (emission, toxins, sea discharge, business licence); implementation unverified. No Israeli annual reporting duty for bakeries or laundries found. Arnona: the only business discount found was the 2020-22 COVID-era scheme (applications closed 31.12.2022); no recurring annual declaration. No Israeli arnona-management software for small businesses was surfaced. Kolzchut clean-air page blocked (403).

result.competitor: ChangeMat by Inbal Data Processing (Beit Zayit): accounting software for currency-exchange businesses. Its company page says it is widely used across Israel and was updated to support Tax Authority and AML authority (IMPA) reporting. Foreign exchange-desk software CurrencyXchanger (Clear View Systems) also offers AML logging, but I found no Israeli adaptation.
result.duty: Confirmed. Income Tax Ordinance s.141A: providers licensed under the Regulated Financial Services Law report every operation of NIS 50,000 or more, with the client's and beneficiary's ID details. Reporting may be no more often than once a quarter. Online filing can be required, and a provider required to file online who doesn't is treated as not having filed. Regulations were published 3.12.2018, and ITA instruction 13/2025 sets financial sanctions; I did not find the sanction amounts. AML identification and reporting duties to IMPA also apply. Licensing is now by the Capital Market Authority (Regulated Financial Services Law s.12(a)), not the old Ministry of Finance Registrar.
result.market: Not verified. The roughly 2,100 registered money changers figure is old and comes from the older Registrar regime. A Forum of financial service providers estimate cited by ice.co.il put Capital Market Authority licensees at about 350 at minimum, across all financial service providers, not only money changers. The 2025 Capital Market Authority report counts 792 credit licensees, a different category. I did not find a current count of financial-asset (currency) licensees.
result.reason: The duty is real. Under Income Tax Ordinance s.141A, licensed financial-asset service providers must report every operation of NIS 50,000 or more. Reports go online, at most once a quarter, and ITA instruction 13/2025 enforces the duty with financial sanctions. But the core job is already done. Inbal Data Processing's ChangeMat is accounting and exchange software built for Israeli money changers. Its company page says it is widely used across Israel and has been updated for reporting to both the Tax Authority and the AML authority (IMPA). Licensing has moved to the Capital Market Authority under the Regulated Financial Services Law. The roughly 2,100 figure is old and unconfirmed; one industry estimate put licensees at about 350 at minimum. A small niche with an entrenched local vendor is weak for a solo founder.

result.competitor: No gemach-specific compliance or reporting software found in Hebrew or English searches. Generic loan-servicing software exists. Nedarim Plus (charedi payments platform) terminals are used to log in to at least one large gemach's member portal (JDN). That makes it a likely competitor or channel; whether it offers a gemach management module was not verified. The Authority's own online upload system handles submission only, not data preparation. Charedi accountants and accounting vendors were not checked (not_reached).
result.duty: Licensing under the Gemach Law (in force 2022). Sector AML order (Prohibition on Money Laundering order for interest-free deposit and credit gemachim, התשפ"ו-2026). Capital Market Authority draft circular (2 Aug 2026; comments due end of August; takes effect 18 months after final publication): written AML/CFT risk policy discussed by the board or management committee, an AML officer, and a yearly report due 31 March in a fixed-template file submitted online, plus separate periodic financial reports (draft circular from Oct 2025: cash flow, donations, deposits, credit, loans in arrears; actuarial opinion for complex gemachim). Penalties not verified. Licensing in practice has been slow: news reports said about 20 of 170+ applications were mature, and the claim says the first 7 licences were issued in Sept 2026 (not independently fetched).
result.market: More than 170 licence applications pending (Knesset committee figures cited by ICE). Gemachim under NIS 1m are exempt. I found no register count of all financial gemachim. The serviceable market is probably a few hundred bodies at most.
result.reason: The duty is real, but parts are not yet in force. The licensing duty is law (in force 2022, per ICE). The sector AML order for gemachim is dated 2026 (התשפ"ו-2026). The Capital Market Authority's risk-management circular was still a draft on 2 Aug 2026 (Calcalist). It takes effect 18 months after final publication and requires a written policy approved by the board, a responsible AML officer, and a yearly report due 31 March in a fixed template uploaded to an online system that rejects files not matching it. In three Hebrew and one English search, plus a check of Nedarim Plus, I found no gemach-specific compliance software. The market is small: about 170 licence applicants. Many are informal, donation-funded charedi bodies that are hard to reach and may not pay much. Nedarim Plus already powers some gemach member portals, so it could become a rival.

result.reason: Duty is real: associations must file annual financial and verbal reports (usually by 30 June) with the Registrar, now partly via online forms. Proper-management certificate lasts 2 years and gates state support and s.46 donation tax credits. Searches found no Israeli product that does the filing, only Green Invoice explainers and foreign nonprofit-software lists. Gaps: the tax-authority software registry covers accounting software, not this filing, and I did not check local vendors. Market is about 37-40k registered associations, but only about 10-15k are truly active. Accountants already handle the work, and small volunteer-run associations pay little. The 2018-2020 guidance may be out of date. Pain and mandatory nature are good, but the price ceiling is low.

result.reason: Duty is real: the Safety at Work Ordinance requires periodic inspection by a chief-inspector-certified inspector for boilers (ss.100-107a), air receivers (ss.113-116), cranes and lifting gear, and lifts. A council procedure (not the law) lists intervals: air receiver 26 months, crane 14 months, lifting accessories 6 months. I did not read the statute, the penalties, or any register count of regulated businesses. The lift bill passed first reading on 29.1.2018 and had not advanced as of the 2022 RIA report. I found no 2024-25 progress, but my search was weak. No Israeli competitor found, but only 4 searches ran and no vendor sites were opened. Safety-officer tools such as K15 likely cover inspection dates. The inspector, not the owner, usually tracks the schedule, so the pain is low. Score stays 3.

The duty looks real but I could not verify its details. The gov.il page (rad-license-request) is the Environmental Protection Ministry's licensing service for medical radiation devices: online application, plan approval, installation, inspection by radiation inspectors, then a licence. WebFetch got 403 on that page, so I only saw it through search snippets. A 2019 Haifa University X-ray permit ran about one year (23/10/2019 to 10/10/2020), under the pharmacists' regulations on radioactive elements (1980). That is a single sample. I did not confirm the statutory renewal cycle, fee, penalties or enforcement. I found no number of dental or X-ray owners. Hebrew searches found no Israeli software; only foreign tools (DOSILINK, DosiServ, SafetyStratus). I did not check local radiation consultancies. Each clinic has few devices, so the need is small and consultancies may already cover it. Score stays at 3.

The licensing law is real and the State Comptroller's June 2026 report discusses the reform. It says about 20.5% of licensable businesses operated without a licence in 2024. I could not confirm the final in-force term table (5/10/15 years) or the 3-month change-reporting duty. Press sources conflict on current terms: 3 vs 5 years for food businesses. The accessibility-proof order was not opened. Longer licence terms (about 10 years for food businesses and salons) cut the recurring renewal trigger, so the duty is weak as a recurring workflow. Searches found no Israeli permit-tracker product, only generic tools (RenewQ). Licensing consultants were not checked. I did not find a register count of licensed businesses. Low frequency and consultant substitutes keep the score low.

Duty is plausible: gov.il says dealing in toxins above thresholds needs a toxins permit under the Hazardous Substances Law 1993, and operating without one is a criminal offence. Search summaries say permit holders must keep purchase and sales ledgers (date, substance, quantity, buyer name and address, buyer signature). I could not open any primary text (gov.il returned 403), and the 1960 Plant Protection sale-licence text is old and possibly superseded. I found no Israeli software for this ledger, but the search was shallow. The market is tiny: probably a few hundred dealers, with unknown counts. The ledger is a low-pain form, and the permit renewal is likely already covered by K03. Score 3.

Duty is real for importers: Ministry of Transport procedure H-02-2019 sets commercial import approval criteria for e-bikes, and SI 15194 is the referenced standard. But it is a per-model, one-off approval, not recurring. The registration and plate duty falls on owners (since 1 Aug 2024), not shops. A municipal PDF gives a 500 NIS fine dated 1.9.25; I could not confirm 750 NIS from 1 Sep 2026. The gov.il page returned 403. The enforcement case I found was from 2015 (mako), not July 2026. I found no software competitor, but the market is a few dozen to a few hundred importers, with no register figure. Shaar Olami and customs brokers likely overlap. Weak recurrence and a small market.

The purchase tax on e-liquid and disposables is real, but it is paid mainly at import and wholesale and has no recurring filing for small retailers that I could find. The draft stock tax on wholesalers (1 NIS/ml, 6 NIS per disposable, only above 10,000 NIS of tax) came from a draft order, and I could not confirm it took effect. The permit and digital-reporting regime for importers and retailers was proposed in the 2026 Arrangements Law, but I found no confirmation it passed. Globes (22 Jul 2026) reported the enforcement legislation stalled when the Knesset dissolved, and that the market is almost entirely black. I found no software or state tool for this, but I ran only one competitor search. The market is small, evasive and shrinking, so willingness to pay is weak. I could not retrieve Chapter 12's text. Score 2.

The duty is real. Employers with 3-9 staff have had to report deposits online since 19 Feb 2023, and those with fewer than 3 since 1 Feb 2025. Sanctions of up to NIS 200,000 are cited, but the sources are old (2016-2018), so the current amount is unverified. The core job is already covered cheaply or free. Payroll bureaus (Malam, Hilan and others) submit the employer-interface file. The Pension Clearing House (Maslaka) reports for about NIS 1 + VAT per ID, per one provider's page. Fund portals, such as Phoenix's, report free and convert manual entry into the file. Payroll software exports the same file. I did not run vendor-specific searches for Tamal or Ranad. A solo founder has no gap to fill. Market size was not found.

Duty is real: gov.il has a carrier licence renewal service and a requirement of up to 5 vehicles under an authorised safety officer or approved safety office, and 6+ under a certified officer. Renewal cycle, fee, penalty and number of carriers were not verified, because the gov.il fetch returned 403. The gov.il renewal page lists food, waste, sewage tanker, hazardous goods and other (4+ vehicles) carriage, so many owner-operators may not need a licence. The digital tachograph is still only being promoted. A Feb 2026 Knesset query says analogue is the current rule, and a 23 Jul 2026 report says regulations are being advanced with a pilot. It is not in force and would hit new trucks only. Competition was not properly checked, and fleet-management and GPS vendors exist. Renewal is infrequent, and a small buyer is hard to reach, so I kept the score low.
